# Stock Market Today (24 October 2026): IDFC First Bank Profit Jumps 196%, Ramky Wins ₹589 Cr Order

 By Gulfam Ansari · Published: Oct 24, 2026, 9:18 PM IST 

 

Indian stocks enter the new week with a fresh set of earnings, orders and corporate actions to track. IDFC First Bank delivered the strongest headline number of the day with a 196% jump in quarterly profit, while Ramky Infrastructure secured a ₹589 crore RVNL order. JK Cement also reported higher profit, AU Small Finance Bank received a positive outlook revision, and Utssav CZ Gold approved a 1:1 bonus issue.

## Today's Key Market Highlights

IDFC FIRST BANK +196% Q2 profit jumps sharply year on year.

RAMKY INFRA ₹589 Cr Wins a major order from RVNL.

JK CEMENT +6.4% Q2 net profit rises year on year.

AU SMALL FINANCE BANK Positive Outlook ICRA improves its outlook on the bank.

...

## IDFC First Bank Q2 Profit Jumps 196%

IDFC First Bank delivered the standout earnings update of the day, with Q2 profit rising 196% year on year. The sharp improvement puts the lender firmly on investors' radar as the banking sector moves through the quarterly results season.

The focus now shifts to the quality of earnings, loan growth, asset quality, margins and deposit trends. A strong profit number is encouraging, but investors will be watching whether the improvement can be sustained over the coming quarters.

Investor takeaway: The 196% profit growth is a strong headline trigger, but the next

...

## Ramky Infrastructure Bags ₹589 Crore RVNL Order

Ramky Infrastructure secured a ₹589 crore order from Rail Vikas Nigam Limited (RVNL), adding a significant fresh contract to its order pipeline.

The order strengthens the company's exposure to railway and infrastructure spending. Investors will track execution timelines, project margins and further order wins as the company works through its growing pipeline.

## JK Cement Q2 Profit Rises 6.4%

JK Cement reported a 6.4% year-on-year increase in Q2 net profit. The result provides a positive earnings signal for the cement maker as the market continues to monitor construction activity, pricing and input costs.

For the coming quarters, cement volumes, realisations, energy costs and capacity utilisation will remain the key factors influencing earnings performance.

...

## AU Small Finance Bank Gets Positive Outlook From ICRA

ICRA upgraded the outlook on AU Small Finance Bank to 'Positive'. The move provides a constructive credit-quality signal for the lender and puts the stock in focus among banking investors.

The outlook change will be assessed alongside the bank's loan growth, asset quality, profitability and funding profile. Investors will also watch whether the positive outlook eventually translates into stronger ratings or improved funding conditions.

...

## Utssav CZ Gold Approves 1:1 Bonus Issue

Utssav CZ Gold Jewels approved a 1:1 bonus issue, giving shareholders an additional share for every share held, subject to the applicable record-date process.

Bonus issues can increase the number of shares held by existing investors without changing the underlying value of their holding at the time of the adjustment. Investors should therefore focus on the company's operating performance rather than treating the bonus itself as a fundamental value creation event.

## Kajaria Ceramics Declares ₹12 Per Share Dividend

Kajaria Ceramics announced a ₹12 per share dividend, adding a shareholder-return trigger to the stock.

Dividend-related developments are particularly relevant for investors tracking companies with established cash-generation and capital-return policies. The record date and payment timeline will be important for eligible shareholders.

## Seshasayee Paper Sales Jump 45%

Seshasayee Paper and Boards reported a strong improvement in quarterly sales, with Q2 sales rising 45%. The sharp increase keeps the paper manufacturer in focus as investors assess demand, realisations and operating margins.

## Ritco Logistics Bags ₹120 Crore Orders

Ritco Logistics secured orders worth approximately ₹120 crore. The fresh business adds to the company's revenue visibility and supports its position in the logistics and transportation segment.

Order execution and the ability to convert new contracts into profitable revenue will remain the key factors to watch.

## Other Important Corporate Updates

- Permanent Magnets: Sees steady demand from the electric-vehicle segment, keeping EV-related growth prospects in focus.
- Panchsheel Organics: Plans to list on the NSE, potentially improving market visibility and liquidity.
- Equippp: Signed an MoU with Instillmotion for a new business collaboration.
- Supreme Power Equipment: Reported a 45% jump in first-half profit.
- Waterbase: Plans to appeal a state tax demand.
- Indian Overseas Bank: RBI revised the bank's CRAR to 19.1%.
- Agribio Spirits: Shareholders approved the proposed merger.
- S V Global Mill: Reported first-half profit of ₹6.3 crore.

---

items.title: Sensex Slips to 73,123 as BPCL Profit Falls 21%, Q2 Earnings Take Centre Stage | PaisaKawach
items.author: PaisaKawach Team
items.text:
Indian equity markets ended the week on a weak note, with the Sensex closing at 73,123.83, down 125.56 points, and the Nifty settling near 22,600, down 0.39%, as persistently high crude oil prices and escalating Middle East tensions kept investors cautious. The broader market fared far worse than the benchmarks — the Nifty Smallcap 100 plunged nearly 3% and the Nifty Midcap 100 fell 2.21%, with roughly 460 of the 500 most-tracked stocks closing in the red.

With the exchanges closed on Saturday, 24 October 2026, the day's business focus has shifted entirely to Q2 FY27 corporate earnings, where a clear divergence is emerging: banks are reporting on credit growth and margin stability, while oil marketing companies are absorbing the margin squeeze from crude prices hovering near six-month highs.

...

## BPCL Q2 Results: Profit Falls 21% as Crude Prices Bite

The most closely watched result of the day came from Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited (BPCL), which reported a 21% year-on-year decline in Q2 net profit to ₹4,863 crore, even as revenue rose nearly 30% year-on-year. EBITDA fell 13.37%, a direct reflection of compressed refining and marketing margins as crude input costs climbed.

### Why BPCL's numbers matter for the wider market

BPCL's results are the first clear earnings-level confirmation of what the market has been pricing in for weeks: high crude oil is not just a macroeconomic headache for India, it is now visibly eroding the profitability of the country's oil marketing companies. With Brent crude closing at $116.72 per barrel on Friday — up 3.14% and near its highest level since April — the pressure on HPCL and IOCL, which report later, is unlikely to ease.

...

## Banking Earnings in Focus: Kotak, AU SFB, IDFC First

Saturday's earnings calendar is dominated by the banking sector, with Kotak Mahindra Bank, AU Small Finance Bank, and IDFC First Bank all scheduled to report Q2 FY27 results. The market will be watching three specific metrics across these lenders.

### What analysts are looking for

After a fortnight of weakness in financial stocks, banking results offer the market its best chance of a positive surprise. However, the macro backdrop — a weak rupee, elevated oil, and a smallcap sell-off — means even strong numbers may struggle to lift sentiment decisively.

- Net interest margins (NIM): With deposit costs still elevated, any compression at Kotak or IDFC First would signal that the rate cycle is hurting lenders more than expected.
- Asset quality: Slippages in unsecured retail and microfinance books — particularly relevant for AU Small Finance Bank — will be scrutinised for early stress signs.
- Credit growth guidance: Commentary on H2 loan growth will matter more than the Q2 print itself, given the market's sensitivity to demand signals.

...

## Other Q2 Results and Pharma Sector Divergence

Beyond banking and oil, today's earnings slate includes JK Cement, Castrol India, Kajaria Ceramics, and Netweb Technologies. In the pharmaceutical space, brokerage HDFC Securities flagged a sharp divergence in recent results: Torrent Pharma's Q2 EBITDA grew 54% year-on-year, driven by the JB Chemicals integration, while Dr. Reddy's saw EBITDA decline 27% year-on-year as US sales fell and India growth failed to offset margin pressure.

---

# Top 10 stocks rated ‘Buy’ this week: Brokerages see 22% to 91% upside

## Brokerages see up to 91% upside in 10 stocks, including Swiggy, KEI Industries and Eternal. Check target prices, Buy ratings and key growth drivers.

Written by Oliviya Kunjumon

 October 24, 2026 06:00 IST 

Brokerages identify 10 stocks with upside potential (Image: Created using Ai)

The Indian stock market ended the week of October 19-23, 2026, with sharp losses. The Sensex fell 2.15%, while the Nifty 50 declined 2.36%, as rising crude oil prices, foreign investor selling and mixed September-quarter earnings weighed on sentiment.

However, brokerage reports identified potential opportunities in 10 stocks, with indicated upside ranging from 22% to 91% based on their target prices.

The 10 stocks covered here have potential upside estimates ranging from 22% to 91%, based on the target prices cited in the reports.

## 1. Swiggy: Nuvama sees 91% upside potential

Nuvama has retained its ‘Buy’ rating on Swiggy, although it has lowered its target price from Rs 444 to Rs 403. The revised target still implies an upside of around 91% from the reference market price used in its report.

According to the brokerage report, Swiggy’s revenue increased 11.1% quarter-on-quarter to Rs 7,570 crore in the September quarter. However, losses widened, with earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) loss reaching Rs 770 crore and net loss standing at Rs 920 crore.

Food delivery contribution margin improved to 7.7%, while Instamart’s contribution margin declined to minus 1%. 

## 2. KEI Industries: Jefferies sees 59% upside potential

Jefferies has a ‘Buy’ rating on KEI Industries and a target price of Rs 6,150, implying an upside of nearly 59% from the reference market price.

According to the global investment bank report, demand for cables and power transmission infrastructure could support growth over the next two years. KEI’s capacity expansion at Sanand, Gujarat, has started commissioning in phases and is expected to contribute to future growth.

“This is a premium to the last 5- year avg of 36x P/E, as visibility on exports and power transmission is improving. Our EPS factors in 20% CAGR over FY26-29E,” it said.

## 3. Vishal Mega Mart: JM Financial sees 49% upside potential

JM Financial has maintained its ‘Buy’ rating on Vishal Mega Mart, with an unchanged target price of Rs 134. This indicates an upside potential of around 49% from the reference price used in its report.

The retailer’s September-quarter performance fell short of expectations. According to JM Financial, EBITDA was 8% below its estimate, while profit after tax missed expectations by 12%. Net profit rose 3.7% year-on-year to Rs 160 crore.

The timing of festivals affected demand during the quarter, with Navratri, Durga Puja and Dussehra shifting into the December quarter. Apparel sales grew 9.5%, compared with 18.2% growth in fast-moving consumer goods (FMCG).

...

## 4. Sobha: Motilal Oswal sees 45% upside potential

Motilal Oswal has retained its ‘Buy’ rating on Sobha and set a target price of Rs 1,710 per share. This represents an upside of around 45% from the reference market price.

According to the brokerage report, Sobha recorded pre-sales of Rs 2,210 crore in the September quarter, up 16% year-on-year. Bengaluru accounted for 60% of bookings, followed by the National Capital Region at 27%.

However, the company also reported lower revenue and profit. Motilal Oswal has highlighted a pipeline of 18 projects covering 20.4 million square feet, with a combined gross development value of Rs 31,400 crore.

...

## 5. Eternal: JM Financial sees 44.2% upside potential

JM Financial has a ‘Buy’ rating on Eternal and a 12-month target price of Rs 450, implying an upside potential of 44.2% from the reference market price.

The brokerage highlighted growth in both Blinkit’s quick-commerce business and Zomato’s food delivery operations. Blinkit’s net order value increased 79.3% year-on-year in the September quarter, while Zomato’s net order value grew 21.5%.

Blinkit’s adjusted EBITDA improved to Rs 1.84 billion, with its margin rising to 0.9% from 0.6% in the previous quarter. The company has also raised its store expansion targets. 

## 6. Crompton Greaves Consumer Electricals: Jefferies sees 41% upside

Jefferies has retained its ‘Buy’ rating on Crompton Greaves Consumer Electricals, with a target price of Rs 305. The target implies an upside of around 41% from the reference market price.

According to the report, Crompton Greaves September-quarter profit after tax was in line with expectations, while sales grew 18% year-on-year and adjusted profit after tax rose 30%.

The company has increased prices in its electrical consumer durables segment to manage higher input costs. 

## 7. Bajaj Finance: Nomura sees 32.7% upside potential

Nomura has maintained its ‘Buy’ rating on Bajaj Finance and set a target price of Rs 1,270, implying an upside potential of 32.7% from the reference market price.

Bajaj Finance September-quarter profit growth was in line with the brokerage’s estimate, and it raised its full-year loan growth guidance. Nomura expects lending growth to remain healthy, with newer businesses such as gold loans adding to the portfolio.

However, higher interest rates could put pressure on net interest margins, which measure the difference between interest earned and interest paid. 

## 8. Oberoi Realty: JM Financial sees 32.1% upside potential

JM Financial has a ‘Buy’ recommendation on Oberoi Realty, with a target price of Rs 2,250. This implies a potential upside of 32.1% from the reference market price.

According to the brokerage report, the Oberoi Realty recorded quarterly pre-sales of Rs 9,150 crore, supported by the launch of Three Sixty North in Gurugram. The project contributed Rs 7,890 crore, with 97% of the launched area booked.

JM Financial expects new projects to support the sales pipeline. 

## 9. ACME Solar Holdings: Nomura sees 26% upside potential

Nomura has initiated coverage on ACME Solar Holdings with a ‘Buy’ rating and a target price of Rs 505, indicating an upside of 26% from the reference market price.

According to the brokerage report, the company is expected to add 4.3 gigawatts of contracted capacity over FY27-FY29. Nomura expects this expansion to support revenue and EBITDA growth over the period.

ACME Solar is also increasing its focus on firm and dispatchable renewable energy, which combines power generation with storage to meet specified delivery schedules. 

## 10. CEAT: Nomura sees nearly 22% upside potential

Nomura has retained its ‘Buy’ rating on CEAT, although it reduced its target price by 6% to Rs 4,009 per share. The revised target implies an upside of nearly 22% from the reference market price.

The tyre maker’s September-quarter revenue was in line with Nomura’s projections, while its EBITDA margin exceeded expectations. However, the brokerage expects raw material prices to rise sequentially in the December quarter, putting pressure on costs.

“It has taken 12-13% price hikes so far in replacement and 14-15% in OE, and more hikes are planned in 3Q. Price hikes by competitors also have been similar with a lag,” Nomura said.

Overall, Swiggy, KEI Industries and Vishal Mega Mart feature among the stocks with the highest indicated upside, while the remaining picks span sectors such as real estate, consumer durables, financial services and renewable energy.

---

- Q2 is expected to be the best QoQ growth quarter (seen in past 3 years), in cc terms, with broad-based growth
- New deal wins in fiscal Q1 at US$461mn were largely in line

 Jefferies On Sona BLW

- Maintain Buy; Hike TP to Rs 900 from Rs 700
- A World of New Opportunities
- Traction motor business is growing strong, and differentials is recovering
- Partnership with Denso and entry into robotics & physical AI opens up big opportunities
- Sona is targeting 10x revenues in 10 years
- Rich multiples should sustain given strong engineering capabilities and growth potential 

Jefferies on IndiGo

- Maintain Buy; Hike TP to Rs 5840 from Rs 5380
- Navigating Turbulence
- Soft JunQ saw high fuel costs only partly offset by strong yield growth
- In FY27, Co has shifted to measured capacity growth, focusing on yields to offset costs
- Despite healthy yields, near term earnings will remain subdued, with a tougher backdrop for peers
- Renewed Middle-East tensions add volatility
- Tight industry supply should support yields & aid FY28 earnings recovery 

Jefferies On Meesho

- Maintain Buy; Hike TP to Rs 240 from Rs 225
- Growth momentum stays strong, with marketplace losses inline
- While balancing value proposition, mgmt. decided to pass on cost inflation
- Outlook remains positive, but a shift in seasonality implies Q2 will be softer, while Q3 should be bumper
- A series of experiments is underway, with aggregate loss within a band

Macquarie On Meesho

- Maintain Underperform with TP of Rs 125
- Sequential growth moderation, margin improvement
- Like Meesho's positioning
- Given its low per-order unit economics, believe the current valuation implies its growth flywheels will remain in overdrive for the next five years

Jefferies On Vishal Mega

- Maintain Buy with TP of Rs 160
- Double Digit SSSG with Margin Expansion
- Slight beat on EBITDA, with double-digit SSSG & GM expansion
- Momentum in store adds continued, with smaller formats also being scaled up
- Own brands remain a key focus, with selective price hikes and no changes to opening price points
- Proposed shareholder approval to cap foreign ownership to <50% signals a potential PE sell-down ahead
